name: The underlying form (aṣl)
definition: The form a word would have by the rule before the changes of iʿlāl, ibdāl and idghām; also, in grammar at large, the default from which other cases depart.
body: Ṣarf explains a form by its aṣl: mīzān is 'in its aṣl' miwzān, madda is madada. The aṣl is a theoretical form the grammarians reconstruct, not something the Arabs are thought to have said. In naḥw the word has a wider use: 'the aṣl of the noun is to be declinable', 'the aṣl of the mubtadaʾ is to come first', so that what departs from it needs a reason; the commentaries say 'against the aṣl' (khilāf al-aṣl) of such cases.

examples.text: The aṣl miwzān and the word mīzān.
